0.long_answer: The condition described is cyclophoria, which is a latent form of heterophoria involving torsional misalignment. In cyclophoria, the eyes tend to rotate about the visual axis (torsion) when normal fusion is disrupted in the absence of appropriate visual stimuli. It is not apparent during binocular viewing because the visual system’s fusion mechanisms normally cancel this latent deviation. This phenomenon is an example of the oculomotor system’s capacity for adaptation, where the latent deviation only becomes evident when fusion is absent or the system is otherwise challenged.
